findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; recorded affinities are removed and the label prior is equal, so no absolute affinity benefit can be read from these observations.

Continuous contrast functions over the observed window are non-monotone: landmark_00_soft_mass shows 4 sign changes with a strong sign conflict and a first-rate z of +9.27 flipping to a last-rate z of -10.00, and landmark_00_local_dy shows 6 sign changes with first-rate z -72.37 flipping to +5.52. A constant rule is therefore not supported; a time-conditioned rule is indicated, but no polynomial was accepted and extrapolation is disallowed.

Branch-adjusted covariance contrasts are weak and mostly null: global_centroid_x/y/z raw covariances have CIs spanning zero (q 0.72, 0.69, 0.97) with same-sign batch fractions near 0.36-0.50, so centroid displacement is not a supported signed contrast.

Shape covariance contrasts are the only branch-adjusted signals approaching significance: shape_yy has a negative whole-window mean with CI entirely below zero (p 0.048, q 0.153, same-sign fraction 0.79) and shape_xx is similarly negative (p 0.096, q 0.232, same-sign fraction 0.79), while shape_zz is null. This is a signed favorable-versus-comparison contrast at the observed nodes, not an absolute geometric descriptor.

hypotheses.falsifier: No sign reversal reproduced under observed-node interpolation, or relative node RMSE not improved over a constant rule.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_00_local_dy contrast values at observed score nodes
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast on landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_00_local_dy, using observed-node interpolation only, better expresses the observed sign reversals than a constant contrast rule.

hypotheses.falsifier: Sign of shape_yy covariance reverses or CI includes zero under additional independent batches.
hypotheses.observable: branch-adjusted raw_covariance of shape_yy at observed nodes
hypotheses.statement: A signed negative shape_yy (and secondarily shape_xx) covariance contrast at the observed selection nodes is a more defensible coordinate direction than centroid displacement.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels or current-study outcome data are supplied, so last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit; the immediate-versus-descendant comparison is unavailable.

No joint-diagnostic, turnover-accounting, increment-effect or endpoint-effect rows were read in this turn, so within-path change versus cohort-composition explanations and joint-versus-marginal coupling remain unassessed.
Contrast curves are coordinate contrasts, not absolute reward targets or physical interaction energies; no neural-module causation is claimed.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters and were not proposed for edit.
